messages.subject: Regarding the LPA models with different parameterization
messages.subject_clean: Regarding the LPA models with different parameterization
messages.body_plain:
Dear TidyLPA Team,

I am a PhD Candidate at Utrecht University and I am analyzing my data using the latent profile analysis. Since it is the first time I am using this analysis, I explored my data using both tidyLPA and mclust packages in R and I have some questions for you. If you have time, I would really appreciate your answer.

Do you maybe know of a good source to better understand models with different parameterization?
Mclust offers 14 different  models and the tidyLPA offers six of them. What is the reason to choose only those six?
Since the authors of mclust talk in terms of shape, volume and orientation and the terms used in tidyLPA are variances and covariances, can someone explain how these terms compare?
I think running the same models in Mplus would help my understanding. Do you maybe have codes to run all these mclust models in Mplus? I am new to Mplus and I am not sure how to use it to run the same models that mclust offers.

Thank you very much in advance.

Kind regards,

Marija Dangubic

messages.subject: Re: Regarding the LPA models with different parameterization
messages.subject_clean: Regarding the LPA models with different parameterization
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marija, thank you for your message. See my responses below (though I welcome others to add to them):

Do you maybe know of a good source to better understand models with different parameterization?

This was a real challenge for me, initially - but think we figured out a way to communicate them effectively. We tried to document the six parameterizations in terms of their covariance matrix as well as verbal descriptions of them here: https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/articles/Introduction_to_tidyLPA.html#model-specification
tidyLPA - data-edu.github.io <https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/articles/Introduction_to_tidyLPA.html#model-specification>
Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) is a statistical modeling approach for estimating distinct profiles, or groups, of variables. In the social sciences and in educational research, these profiles could represent, for example, how different youth experience dimensions of being engaged (i.e., cognitively, behaviorally, and affectively) at the same time.
data-edu.github.io <http://data-edu.github.io>

Mclust offers 14 different  models and the tidyLPA offers six of them. What is the reason to choose only those six?

These are the six most common parameterizations. Indeed, for LPA, often, only one (what in tidyLPA is the first model type - Equal variances, and covariances fixed to 0.

Since the authors of mclust talk in terms of shape, volume and orientation and the terms used in tidyLPA are variances and covariances, can someone explain how these terms compare?

See the link above.

I think running the same models in Mplus would help my understanding. Do you maybe have codes to run all these mclust models in Mplus? I am new to Mplus and I am not sure how to use it to run the same models that mclust offers.

You can simply change the package argument (for estimate_profiles), as follows, to run them in MPlus:

m <- pisaUSA15[1:100, ] %>%
    single_imputation <https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/reference/single_imputation.html>() %>%
    estimate_profiles <https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/reference/estimate_profiles.html>(2, package = "MplusAutomation") %>%
    compare_solutions <https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/reference/compare_solutions.html>(statistics = c <https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/topics/c>("AIC", "BIC"))

It may need some processing, but, the Mplus model code would then be saved to the `m` object; you can access it via:

> m$model_1_class_2$model$input

--

messages.subject: Variations in outcomes TidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
Dear members,
I am currently exploring the TidyLPA package in R studio for the first time to get aquiainted with the approach. I really like the possibilities it provides. However, I do have a question: I noticed that when I ran the same script several times, this resulted in different outcomes. For instance, the entropy value varied from about 0.56 to 0.42 (both not good - I know - it was just an exploration). Can you explain where such differences come from? How should this affect my interpretations? I hope you can find time to clarify this so I can understand the package better.
Kind regards, Annemieke Smale

messages.subject: Re: Variations in outcomes TidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Annemieke,

Are you using the default package (if you aren't passing a package argument, this is the case; I'm curious whether you are adding package = 'MplusAutomation' or package = 'mplus' (either work).

In short, this matters because the two potential packages ('mclust' or 'MplusAutomation') have slight differences in how the estimation works. For mclust, first, a hierarchical cluster analysis is carried out, and then the results of the clustering are used to provide starting values for the maximum likelihood estimation. For mplus, random starting values are used, but a number of starts are run, and then the fitted model associated with the lowest log-likelihood is considered to be the model used for/presented in the output.

So, knowing about which package you are using will at least help me/us to zero in on what may be going on.

Best,
Josh

--

Dear members,
I am currently exploring the TidyLPA package in R studio for the first time to get aquiainted with the approach. I really like the possibilities it provides. However, I do have a question: I noticed that when I ran the same script several times, this resulted in different outcomes. For instance, the entropy value varied from about 0.56 to 0.42 (both not good - I know - it was just an exploration). Can you explain where such differences come from? How should this affect my interpretations? I hope you can find time to clarify this so I can understand the package better.
Kind regards, Annemieke Smale

messages.subject: Duplicate warning in TidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
One more rookie-question... In my analyses with the TidyLPA package I keep getting warnings about duplicate rows (that are not used in the analyses). It is not clear to me why duplicates are found; the row names (column names in Excel) obviously vary.
I tried to get around this problem by using random numbering as rownames (by using the command ->  rownames (data) = rep (1:2066) ) but I still get this warning. Any suggestions?
Kind regards, Annemieke Smale
